summary: Milestone M3 (Validation, intake and routing) verified across its four documented steps (M3-S01..M3-S04) with M3-S05 blocked on deferred Q32-Q35 and left blocked. Verdict not-ready, on three independent grounds: a blocked step; a declared milestone acceptance test that exits 1 (F-29, check_custom_permissions.py --strict fails on a CP-DESC-02 description-length WARN against M2-S01's already-accepted custom permission, a rule that landed in commit f5c7ce8ea after the test was declared); and step manifests disagreeing on the API version (F-31, 62.0 on M3-S01/S02 vs 67.0 on M3-S03/S04). 41 of 41 cross-artefact references resolve, 0 unresolved and 0 unclassifiable; all five operator-named cross-checks pass, including routing-address caseOrigin subset, assignment-rule queue subset, folder-qualified auto-response template, object-qualified newEntityRecordType subset, and no senderEmail/replyToEmail equal to a routing address. No deploy-order contradiction. Merged manifest written at 6 types / 8 members, no member collision, no unmanifested deployable file, version conflict reported in-file rather than resolved silently. Three of four executable/structural milestone tests pass. Two further findings: F-30, M3-S02's sender note and M3-S04's metadata name different acknowledgement senders so manual test B06 is not tickable as written; F-32, the Web-to-Case channel's dependence on the bypass grant is documented in M3-S03's deploy-order but reaches no checklist, elevated. F-33 LOW, a stale sentence in M3-S03 deploy-order section 6. Verdict recorded as set-milestone --status rejected. No org was contacted, no sf command and no mock_deploy.py run, nothing deployed, and G3 is left to the human.
confidence_rationale: Step 10 rubric, LOW branch, on its first named trigger: a step was blocked (M3-S05). That is the binding constraint and it would hold even if everything else were clean. Two independent facts would also have capped this below HIGH: a declared milestone acceptance test failed rather than merely warning, and the merged manifest carried a version conflict that was reported rather than resolved (the MEDIUM branch's second clause). Nothing in the reference resolution pulled it down - 41 of 41 references resolved with zero unclassifiable, which is the one dimension this run covered completely. LOW here measures how much of M3 the checks could see, not how badly the milestone is built: four of five steps are documented, tested and documented again, and 42 of 42 components validated live in mock-deploy Run 6 bar the one org-side sender address.

findings.title: Declared milestone test M3-T2 exits 1 on a description-length advisory about an already-accepted M2 artefact
findings.detail: python3 skills/admin/custom-permissions/scripts/check_custom_permissions.py --manifest-dir artefacts --strict exits 1 against a declared exit 0. The only finding is CP-DESC-02, a WARN: artefacts/M2-S01/customPermissions/Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation.customPermission-meta.xml carries a 250-character description against a 200-character advisory threshold and a 255-character documented platform limit (api_meta L46651). --strict makes every WARN blocking. CP-DESC-02 did not exist when the test was declared: git log -S'CP-DESC-02' places it in commit f5c7ce8ea, the skill-hardening wave that closed mock-deploy F-15. MILESTONE-M2-REPORT-v2.md F-16 anticipated it verbatim, listing 'the 250-character CustomPermission description ... which no checker reads'. One now does. Not a metadata defect: 250 < 255 and the file validated live in mock-deploy runs 2, 3, 5 and 6. The positive half of the test still passes on its merits - coverage row 'Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation 2 permission set Case_Intake_Integration', the two consumers being M3-S01's two validation rules.
findings.recommendation: Shorten M2-S01's description below 200 characters and re-run M3-T2 (immediate, one string, closes M2's half-open F-16 headroom item at the same time), and fix the checker's exit policy so CP-DESC-02 stays advisory under --strict - exactly the remedy commit 214da9abd already applied to check_access_model.py for the identical failure shape. Do NOT drop --strict from M3-T2: it was declared to make an unresolvable-consumer-reference WARN blocking, which is the assertion the test exists for.

findings.title: Step manifests disagree on the API version; the build carries no plan-level version field
findings.detail: artefacts/M3-S01/package.xml and artefacts/M3-S02/package.xml declare 62.0; artefacts/M3-S03/package.xml and artefacts/M3-S04/package.xml declare 67.0. Every M1 and M2 manifest, and both earlier merged milestone manifests, read 62.0. The merged M3 manifest carries 67.0 with the disagreement named in an XML comment rather than silently resolved. 62.0 is not a live option: mock-deploy Run 4 probes (a) and (b) proved newEntityRecordType is rejected at 62.0 and 63.0 and accepted from 64.0, and Runs 5 and 6 deployed at 67.0. agents/milestone-verifier/AGENT.md lists an API-version disagreement under REFUSAL_NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW; this run did not refuse because Step 5 of the same playbook gives an explicit in-report handling for the case, and refusing would have suppressed the five other G3 decision items. findings.title: The Web-to-Case channel's dependence on the bypass grant is documented but reaches no checklist line
findings.detail: artefacts/M3-S03/deploy-order.md section 6 records that both intake channels rely on Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation to pass M3-S01's rules, that the Permission Set carrying it (Case_Intake_Integration, M2-S01) must be assigned to the identity the channels save as, and that assignment is an org action outside this build - and that if the identity cannot hold it, 'every intake save fails ... a rejection the submitter never sees, because the web form still returns its retURL success page'. After the F-26/F-27 rebuild the exposure narrowed to one channel, and section 0 of the same file says so: email cases arrive with Origin stamped and Priority Medium so neither rule fires; web cases arrive with Origin Web stamped but Priority blank, because WebToCaseSettings has no priority element (three children, api_meta L112128 ff.). So at the end of M3, with M4 not built, Priority_Required_On_Agent_Save fires on every Web-to-Case submission (~60/day) unless the web save identity holds the bypass. M4-S03's before-save flow would also close it - before-save record-triggered flows run ahead of custom validation rules - but that step is pending and is itself subject to G3 decision item 2. Appears in no skipped_manual[] line in any tests/<step>/results.json.
findings.recommendation: Elevated to manual checklist line 9. Before G3 is signed, someone confirms the identity Web-to-Case saves as can hold and has been assigned Case_Intake_Integration - or the gate records that Web-to-Case intake is knowingly at risk until M4-S03 stamps Priority. Choosing G3 item 2 option (2) closes this by flow rather than by assignment.

process_observations.observation: The M3-S03 rebuild is the cleanest loop in this build so far. Three org rejections (F-25, F-26, F-27) were each isolated on a scratchpad copy before any artefact moved, fixed with exactly four changes and nothing else, hash-recorded before and after, and each one also produced a named skill-side remedy rather than only a build-side patch. F-26 in particular converted 'gotcha 9 instructs writing newEntityRecordType' into two facts the guide does not carry - an API 64.0 floor and the object-qualified value form - both marked UNVERIFIED-in-guide / proven-live.

M3-S04's builder declined to write the Account-support-tier criterion rather than invent a cross-object criteriaItems notation, and named F-26 as the precedent for why guessing a value shape costs a rebuild. The omission was recorded as a decision with the mismatch it creates, which is why the gate can see it at all.

This is the third checker in the same family to fail a milestone on a description-length advisory because --strict is all-or-nothing: check_access_model.py at M2 (fixed in 214da9abd by scoping the blocking set), and now check_custom_permissions.py at M3. M2's own report predicted this exact artefact would be next. A --strict that cannot be scoped by severity turns every new advisory rule into a retroactive gate failure on already-accepted artefacts.

The operator's pre-gate amendment on M3-S04 propagated correctly into the metadata, the auto-response XML comment, the workbook row and four decisions entries - but not back into M3-S02's sender-identity-note.md, which is where the B06 gate checklist actually lives. A decision made downstream of a document leaves that document as the stale copy, and the checklist is the artefact a human reads at the gate (F-30).

tests/M3-S03/results.json lists three entries in ran[] and omits check-outputs, while the same step's tester envelope (envelopes/M3-S03/2026-09-12T04-53-23Z.json) reports check-outputs ok. The results file is the machine-readable record; the envelope is the narrative one. They should not disagree about what ran.

REQ-022 ('Tier 1 should get work pushed to them when they are available') resolves in traceability.md against Queue:Tier_1_General from M2-S04, so the matrix shows no coverage gap while the push capability itself is unbuilt and blocked in M3-S05. The row is not wrong - the queue is a real delivery against part of the requirement - but a reader trusting the RTM's green would not learn that the verb in the requirement has no artefact anywhere in the plan.

Three component types in this milestone have no slot in the ten-position deploy sequence - ValidationRule, EmailFolder and EmailTemplate - joining BusinessProcess and CustomPermission from earlier milestones. The doc keeper handled each the same honest way, reporting the gap and placing the component by its own dependency chain instead. Five instances is enough to suggest the sequence itself is short a few positions rather than each step being an exception.

Checked as the Output Contract requires: plan.json carries no scale field at all (scale is null), so there is no recorded value for the D/S/O/X counts to disagree with. Nothing to flag as an unrecorded override - but equally, no recorded sizing for this five-milestone, 22-step build to be held to.
